name: runtime-array-parity
goal: The unshipped kernel closure candidate returns the c767 output for every input portableJson and kernelRequest admit, including in-memory arrays with their own iterator or species

steps.title: Identify the regression, prior working behavior, root cause, and evidence.
steps.evidence: Regression in the unshipped v3 candidate (src/utils/kernelClosure.ts sha256 11e34c72, not pre-existing): two requests that portableJson and kernelRequest admit unchanged now give other output on the module path. Prior behaviour, c767 (sha256 45b5eac7): (1) edge [1,0] with its own Symbol.iterator yielding 0,1, nodes a,b, base=head, changed=sinks=[a]: affected [a]; v3 gives [a,b]. (2) nodes a,b of an Array subclass whose Symbol.species makes arrays that iterate nothing, no edges: affected [], unknown [a]; v3 gives affected [a], unknown []. A JSON round trip gives [a,b] and affected [a] in both versions. Root cause: v3 replaced destructuring each edge through its iterator with edge[0]/edge[1] reads, and new Map over the species-created nodes.map result with nodes.forEach and set(). Admission accepts any Array.isArray value, and the earlier 246-text and 150x2 parity serialized every input, so no in-memory array reached the closure. Evidence: independent array review and rejected contract review; reproduction log cases-v0-v3.log sha256 96020fe6.

steps.title: Propose a root-cause repair and an automated guard for the identified failure.
steps.evidence:
Repair: return indexGraph to c767 byte for byte; no exact fast path exists. An exact per-edge guard (read Symbol.iterator once, then length, 0, length, 1 as the array iterator does) cost the same as destructuring, 101.7-103.7 against 100.8-103.5 us min for both graphs (instrumentation only, log edge-guard-cost.log sha256 4219c04a); v3 reads cost 47.7-48.1. It also changes error text on stateful inputs and cannot cover new Map over a species-made array without extra observable reads, so it was rejected as fragile and no cheaper. Alternative internal cost improvement, exact for every input because it touches only the closure's own Maps, Int32Arrays and Set: merge builds each answer once (nearest and farthest of the two distances, seed inline) instead of a two-item array, filter, Math.min spread and a {...node, seed} copy. Guard: the two unchanged regression tests in test/utils/impact-kernel.test.ts (default vitest include, run by test:unit and check), plus one AGENTS.md rule asking for admission characterization before serialization.
Reopened 2026-10-15T22:06:10.614Z: newly demonstrated admitted mapped-array out-of-range index disproves c1b nonnegative distance assumption; retained prior evidence is historical, not clearance.
Final repair 2026-10-15T22:10:23.920Z: Use the original >=0 exclusion separately for base/head distances, including undefined from admitted mapped-array out-of-range indices. Neither included returns no node; both included choose Math.min; one included retains its value and direction. Build answer once with seed; indexing and all admitted input reads unchanged. Retain public iterator/species regressions and add three admitted map-index rows covering neither/base/head distances. No admission narrowing or global built-in patches.

Variant c1 (sha256 880a7746, complexity 32, 4182 bytes) passed the same proofs and was superseded by this smaller one; every version is kept byte-exact with hashes. Guard wired: test/utils/impact-kernel.test.ts is in the default vitest include used by test:unit and check. AGENTS.md gains one rule under Required Harness Workflow. Observational budget measure: source-bytes 4096 (ledger 4057), complexity 30 (29), dependencies 1 (1); the growth needs root review. Instrumentation only, never a benchmark: kernelClosure on graph-1k about 25-37 us below c767 min, v3 about 75-80.
